stemMd: For the neutral atoms sodium and chlorine in the same period, which general comparison is expected?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Chlorine has the larger radius because it has more protons.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Atomic radius is independent of nuclear attraction.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Sodium has the larger atomic radius.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Their radii must be identical because they share a period.

explanationMd: Across a period, increasing effective nuclear attraction draws the electron cloud inward. Sodium, towards the left, is generally larger than chlorine despite the same principal occupied-shell count.

distractorRationale.e: A shared number of shells does not imply identical radius.
distractorRationale.a: Greater effective nuclear attraction generally contracts atoms across the period.
